message.text: Message delivery: automatic. Servex hands me every prompt you speak on any card, plus the task and error events, and the fast assistant passes nothing on. The same prompt also goes to that card's own assistant. Session length: I'd start fresh from an always-current handoff file, since the repo already has one at ai/handover.md, and keep it updated as we go so losing a session costs nothing.

I don't know how messages reach the master assistant, and I won't guess. I've asked the manager to check the code and answer both questions: how long a session should live, and how messages get relayed.

Lifetime: no session lives forever. Idle assistants and managers are stopped after about 10 minutes, the master after 15, and helpers after 3, and each resumes by its session id on the next message. Card agents can be rebuilt: they write a summary line into the card log and restart from it. The master, the mastermind and the fast assistant have no handoff file, and the fast assistant loses its session on every Servex boot. The smallest fix is one append-only state file per agent, added to a fresh session's first prompt.

Relay: it's automatic and doesn't depend on the fast assistant passing anything on. Each sentence you speak becomes a prompt line. If a card is selected, that card's own assistant answers. Otherwise the fast assistant files it onto a card. The master hears every prompt once it reaches a card, batched to at most once per 20 seconds, but a prompt left only on the prompts log never reaches it. The mastermind hears only what another agent sends it.

message.text: Sent to mastermind-servex for the Prompt mechanics manager: dictate and chat treated as two parts, raw transcript kept with headings and paragraphs beside it, the jumpy text box, a possible prompt-interpretation assistant, done checkboxes, the extra padding and the resize bug.

Handed to the manager as one list: named headings for long dictation while keeping the raw text, the jumpy text area, a possible prompt-interpreter agent, done checkboxes and clickable sub-cards, the extra right padding, and the resizer moving both sidebars.

Split agreed with mastermind-servex. Two minions are on my part now. One fixes the card page (extra right padding, the resizer that moves both chat sidebars, done checkboxes and clickable sub-cards). The other adds smart chat scroll and extracts the chat into a reusable ext/Chat. The prompt-mechanics-2 manager takes the dictation work: long dictation shown as chat bubbles with the raw transcript kept, the jumpy live text, and the paragraph and heading structuring. Your idea of a separate prompt-interpretation agent isn't started. For now I'd suggest the manager does that work, because a second always-on agent adds cost and needs its own state.

Smart chat scroll is in, as a reusable module at /framework/ext/Chat/. A new message follows you while you're at the bottom, holds still once you scroll up, and follows again when you scroll back down. It was proven headless and on a real card, and AI 2 now uses it, so it's linked from the ext index and has a readme, demo page and a scroll doc. Two things to know: the folder also holds Composer.js and Mic.js from the other manager's half-built start, which I haven't reviewed, and the card layout fixes are still in progress.

The card page fixes are in: the extra right padding is gone, the resizer moves only its two neighbouring columns, and card pages load with no errors (checked at 3440 wide, where five columns appear). Sub-card lists now show a ticked box and a struck-through title for done items, and each item is clickable. The tick styling was checked in a picture, but no sub-card is marked done in the real data yet, so seeing it live needs one to be marked done. Please reload and try the resizer.

Layout reconciled on every card: chat as the right-hand column, one chat scroll area, no void, textarea cap removed from Chat.css. One caveat: Mic.js still caps the box at about 12 lines. That belongs to the dictation manager, and I've asked for it to be lifted.
